gloss: plant division (horticulture); dividing a plant at the root

definitions.gloss: dividing a plant at the root; plant division; root division
definitions.explanation: A method of propagating plants by digging up an established clump and splitting its root mass into two or more sections, each of which is replanted as a new individual. Used for many perennials, grasses, and houseplants that grow in clumps.

examples.english: To divide a plant at the root.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}に{株分|かぶわ}けをすると{元気|げんき}に{育|そだ}つ。
examples.english: If you divide it in spring, the plant will grow vigorously.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}が{庭|にわ}の{花|はな}を{株分|かぶわ}けして、{隣|となり}の{人|ひと}にも{分|わ}けた。
examples.english: My mother divided the flowers in the garden and gave some to the neighbors.

examples.japanese: このアロエは{株分|かぶわ}けで{簡単|かんたん}に{増|ふ}やせるので、{初心者|しょしんしゃ}にもおすすめだ。
examples.english: This aloe can be easily propagated by division, so it's recommended even for beginners.

notes:
Composed of {株|かぶ} (the root or base of a plant; a clump) + {分|わ}け (division, from the verb {分|わ}ける to divide). A standard method of plant propagation in which an overgrown clump is carefully dug up and split at the roots into several smaller plants.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {株分|かぶわ}けをする: to perform root division
- {株分|かぶわ}けで{増|ふ}やす: to propagate by division
- {春|はる}の{株分|かぶわ}け: spring division
- {株分|かぶわ}けに{適|てき}した{時期|じき}: the right season for root division

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {挿|さ}し{木|き}: cutting — propagation by rooting a piece of stem or branch, rather than dividing the root mass.
- {取|と}り{木|き}: layering — propagation by bending a branch down to the soil so it grows its own roots before being separated.
- {接|つ}ぎ{木|き}: grafting — joining a shoot of one plant onto the rootstock of another.

USAGE:
A common word in gardening magazines, plant-care guides, and nursery labels. {株分|かぶわ}け is typically recommended for hostas, ornamental grasses, irises, daylilies, ferns, and many succulents. The best time of year depends on the species, but early spring and autumn are most common.
